subject: Orion reserved capacity — capacity lock & flex-credit ask
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@orion.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orion reserved capacity proposal and price protection

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a concise proposal that maps Orion's expected peak inference load to a 12‑month reserved GPU commitment. Key points up front:

- Proposed commit: 80 reserved A100-equivalent slots (phased over Q3)
- Baseline discount (vs on-demand): 36%
- Conditional flex credit pool: 10% of committed tokens that can be burned as burst credits (applies only during short-term spikes)
- Pricing trigger: mid-term GPU indexation clause tied to market benchmark; we can cap pass-through at +12% YoY without triggering re-negotiation.

Attachments: Orion_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx (workload assumptions & monthly ramp), Orion_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft).

Before I lock this in with legal, a couple asks from our side:
1) Can Orion confirm a primary point of contact for procurement (contracts@) and the target signature timeline (we recommended 30 days)?
2) Would Orion consider a 9‑month phase‑in for full capacity (we can enable phased billing to reduce sticker shock)?

I know you mentioned concern about GPU price volatility — if you can share a simple target (e.g., max pass-through % or a preference for credits vs price caps), I can escalate internally and propose an approval path.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri y.om.das@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

(Attached: Orion_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx, Orion_SOW_v1.pdf)

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@orion.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: orion-contracts@orion.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orion reserved capacity proposal and price protection

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the proposal and the worksheets — very helpful. A few follow-ups from our finance and infra teams:

- We like the phased approach. For cashflow reasons we prefer 6 months to reach full utilization rather than 9.
- On GPU price volatility: our procurement policy requires either a fixed-floor/fixed-cap structure or an explicit credit bucket if vendor prices rise >10% year-over-year.
- If Redwood can commit to a price-protection mechanism (either a credit pool that grows with realized spend or a 1‑year price cap not exceeding +8%), we can push for an accelerated sign-off.

Also, can you confirm whether the flex credits are refundable if unused at the end of the contract, or if they simply expire? That will impact our evaluation.

Best,
Priya Singh
Head of Procurement | Orion AI
priya.singh@orion.ai

Team —

Forwarding Orion's ask (below). They are asking for one of two options:
A) a credit bucket that scales with realized spend (refundable if unused at term end)
B) a 1-year price cap no greater than +8% if market GPU costs increase.

Numbers: 80 A100-eq reserved, baseline discount 36%, flex credits 10% of committed tokens. They prefer a 6-month phase-in.

What I need: an approval path or recommended counter. Finance (Kim) — can we support refundable credits in the SOW? Ben — any commercial precedent for a short-term cap vs a credit pool? Marcus — want to flag because anything above a small concession will need exec sign-off.

I attached the sizing worksheet and SOW for reference.

Thanks,
Priyom

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orion reserved capacity proposal and price protection — request for approval path

Priyom / Ben —

Reviewed the worksheet and SOW. Summary of finance stance:
- We can offer a refundable flex-credit bucket up to 6% of committed spend (applies only to unused burst credits at term conclusion) subject to a minimum utilization covenant (65% averaged over months 7–12).
- Alternatively, a hard price cap of +8% for year 1 is possible, but only if Orion takes a 15% higher commit (i.e., 92 A100-eq) or agrees to a 24-month contract instead of 12.
- Any refundable credits higher than 6% or a cap stricter than +8% requires Marcus' exec sign-off.

Recommendation: Offer the refundable 6% credit bucket + 6-month phase-in. This keeps commercial exposure bounded and meets Orion halfway. If Orion insists on a strict +8% cap with 12-month term, escalate to Marcus for approval.

Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

4) We attached an updated SOW (Orion_SOW_v1.pdf) with the credit mechanics and utilization covenant called out.
